correctness.rationale: For odd abelian A every subgroup either lies in A or is unique H(B,x)=B rtimes <xt>, parameterized by B<=A and x+B. All kernel subgroups are normal. Exact semidirect multiplication gives H(B,x)H(C,y)=H(C,y)H(B,x) iff x-y in B+C, since the odd quotient has no nonzero 2-torsion. For each B,C there are exactly |A:B intersect C| compatible coset pairs. This yields sd=(ell^2+2ell omega+eta)/(ell+omega)^2. The subspace-intersection counting identity gives the stated Gaussian triple sum and constrained exponent optimization yields parity: even r>=2 tends 1/4; odd r>=3 tends 3/p; r=1 is (7p+9)/(p+3)^2. Independent exact fractions for p=3 and r=1,2,3,4 were 5/6,34/49,3239/5618,18433/36963. Finite tests support but do not prove the general formulas.

originality.rationale: 2018 relative subgroup-commutativity full texts and the 2023 polygroups context concern ordinary cyclic-kernel dihedral or general identities. A highly relevant full published dicyclic analogue treats generalized dicyclic groups with a nontrivial involution y in the abelian kernel; its even-kernel setting and its (xz^-1)^2 in BC criterion do not include odd generalized dihedral kernels directly. No dominating formula or identical fixed-rank parity asymptotic was found.
residual_risks: The full 2009 Journal of Algebra paper was not separately read in this run; equivalence under older semidirect notation is a residual literature risk.
The nearby generalized dicyclic all-kernel theorem is analogous but does not cover odd involution-split groups.
Asymptotics hold for fixed rank p->infinity; odd A is essential.
